body.statement: Using \(\mathsf H_{\rm prof}\), determine the explicit piecewise function \(r_{n,K}(a,\beta)\) and the maximal \(\kappa_{\max}\) such that \(\rho^\star_{n,K}(a,\epsilon_{\rm tot})\asymp r_{n,K}(a,\beta)\) uniformly whenever \(K\le n^{\kappa_{\max}}\). Derive the exact transition surfaces obtained by balancing \(r_{\rm dense}\), \(r_{\rm tail}\), \(r_{\rm train}\), and the least-favorable active-face scale \(r_{\rm face}\). The formula must agree with the fixed-\(K\) upper bound and, if the legal dense construction is established, must not fall below \(r_{\rm dense}\) in that construction's regime.
body.justification: The piecewise radius is the paper's named theorem-level focal object.
body.gap: Breunig and Chen characterize structural-space NPIV testing, and Marteau and Sapatinas characterize a diagonal Gaussian sequence experiment; neither result determines this observed-image radius.
body.consumer: The frontier converts support size and proxy strength into a checkable detectability limit for discrete one-NCO diagnostics.
